Alfalfa Symposium Proceedings – ET Before Cutting
Last alfalfa irrigation before harvest; criteria for stopping and reducing water

Practical criterion for stopping alfalfa irrigation before harvest: drainage of about 2 inches ET between the last irrigation and cutting in silt loam soil; growing-season consumption over 0.30 and fall consumption about 0.10 inches per day. Key point: alfalfa has no critical water-stress stage, but moisture between cuts must be controlled.
Can alfalfa regrow after irrigation is stopped before harvest?
Yes. Alfalfa, unlike many crops, has no specific critical growth stage for water stress; under drought it enters dormancy and resumes growth after moisture returns.
How much ET drainage is needed before cutting?
In silt loam soils of southern Idaho, about 2 inches of cumulative ET after irrigation and before cutting has been reported as sufficient for adequate soil drying.
What is the purpose of fall irrigation?
Fall irrigation through November (before freeze-up) can provide deep water reserves for rapid spring growth next year; the goal is water storage, not maximizing yield in the current season.
